notes: Static read-only audit only: I did not execute tests, compute hashes, or access the repository; approval rests on static review of the supplied source plus internally consistent supplied evidence (manifest/tests-passed.json/parent-gates.json hash agreement; 3219 passed macOS + 3219 passed Linux aarch64; 539 targeted passed; lint clean; all parent probes exit 0).

Trust boundary: exact-type validation, content-hash and grant/source/destination cross-binding, deepcopy-on-read defenses, and no request/event.raw/model-derived authority are all present; no loader, route, env switch, or background refresh exists and none is claimed.

Coherent-check design correctly denies mixed views (state identity + epoch fence), concurrent refresh/invalidate during a pass (including during the final stopped()/clock callbacks), reentrant/cross-thread pin borrowing, and stale/future/rollback clock cases with permanent per-instance latch.

Retention source/grant/snapshot deadlines are unaffected by authority refresh (separate ledger; test_completed_job_retention_and_budgets_never_renew_on_refresh); A10 ordering (retention SQL before the entire mirror, no authority mutex across SQL) is preserved and probed.

Minor hardening gap (fail-closed, non-blocking): AuthoritySnapshot._freeze rejects ':' in principal.actor_id but not in principal.platform; a colon in platform yields a 4-field permission string that grants._permission_levels rejects as malformed, so no privilege escalation path, but an explicit symmetric check would be tidier.

create_service intentionally requires exact BriefStore and non-None GenerationConfig (stricter than the legacy BriefService constructor); retention wiring is validated via configure_guard with concrete RetentionGuard target identity.
No production source loader, model deployment, or enabled lifecycle claims are made in code or docs; module docstrings explicitly disclaim them, consistent with the slice's stated limits.
